anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Physical read/write demand exceeds the throughput, IOPS, or latency capacity of the underlying storage volumes, making the storage layer the immediate performance bottleneck.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume an abnormally high share of host CPU cycles, driving the CPU subsystem into sustained saturation.

When both anomalies strike simultaneously, the database shows a blended symptom set: device-level queues are full while OS run queues are equally backed up; read, write, and durability wait events climb together with scheduler and spin waits; statement response times and batch windows expand non-linearly; CPU-bound sessions may stall waiting on I/O completions, yet once I/O returns they compete for already exhausted CPU, causing saw-tooth latency patterns. Monitoring dashboards reveal near-100 % CPU utilization alongside storage latency spikes, but it becomes difficult to attribute delays to a single layer because every execution phase—parsing, execution, logging, checkpointing—encounters both CPU and I/O contention.

Causally, the two root causes reinforce each other: slow storage elevates CPU demand by extending every I/O-bound code path, keeping worker threads active longer, increasing context switches, and driving up spin and latch activity. Conversely, CPU saturation lengthens I/O submission and completion processing, inflates interrupt handling time, and can starve the I/O scheduler of CPU, which further degrades effective throughput. Maintenance tasks or poorly tuned queries may first saturate CPU, pushing checkpoints and log flushes into backlog, which then overruns the storage bandwidth; or a storage degradation event may prolong synchronous I/Os, causing threads to pile up and flood the CPU once data finally arrives. The vicious feedback loop magnifies individual impacts, ultimately crippling both compute and storage subsystems and making traditional single-bottleneck tuning ineffective.

entry.official_definition: Read timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol read operation exceeds mysqlx_read_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network read operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
